# Charlotte Preparatory School — Financial Aid and Tuition — Financial Support

Charlotte Prep calls its financial aid "tuition assistance". It is offered for Kindergarten through 8th grade and is awarded on need, merit and fit. The school states two different application deadlines on the same page. This file sets out what the school publishes, and what it does not, as of October 19, 2026. The source page is https://charlotteprep.org/admissions/tuition-fees.

### Who can get it, and on what basis

- **Grades:** "Tuition assistance is offered in grades K-8th". The school does not offer it for its Montessori programs below Kindergarten (Pre-Primary, Primary and Transitional Kindergarten).
- **Basis:** "Tuition assistance is awarded on the basis of financial need, academic merit, and the student's fit with our Charlotte Prep missions and vision."
- **How need is measured:** "Tuition assistance is determined through analysis of a family's financial resources, including income and assets. To determine fair and equitable assistance awards, Charlotte Preparatory School subscribes to the principles and needs analysis system of the Clarity application."
- **Every year:** "Each family applying for financial assistance must complete all application procedures annually by the renewal deadlines and continue to demonstrate comparable financial eligibility to receive assistance."
- **Confidential:** "Yes, all applications for tuition assistance are held in the strictest confidence."
- **Families abroad can apply:** through Clarity, with the Non-US Tax Filer Verification upload. Canadian families upload their T1, T4 and Notice of Assessment.

### How to apply

The school lists these steps:
1. "Make a formal request in writing or via email to the attention of the Director of Enrollment." That is Seher Khanna, skhanna@charlotteprep.org.
2. Complete the Clarity application at https://auth.clarityapp.com/en/signup/.
3. Use Clarity's guides, which the school links: a Quick Reference Guide, a Family Application Guide, and Spanish versions of each.

**Clarity's own fee.** Clarity's quick-reference guide says "The app fee is $60 per household and covers all the Clarity schools to which you are applying." This is Clarity's figure, from its 2025/2026 guide. Charlotte Prep's page does not state it.

### The deadline: the page gives two different dates

Both statements are on the same live page:

| Where on the page | What it says |
|---|---|
| Main text, "Tuition Assistance" | "We recommend you apply by January 2; applications received after the deadline will still be considered as long as funds are available." The steps repeat it: "Apply by January 2 prior to the enrollment year." |
| FAQ, "When do I need to apply?" | "You must submit your full completed application by January 15." |

Both come from https://charlotteprep.org/admissions/tuition-fees, retrieved October 19, 2026.

The likely reason: in November 2024 the main text and the FAQ both said January 15. The main text has since moved to January 2, which is the same date as the Early School and Kindergarten application deadline. The FAQ was not updated. Until the school resolves it, applying by January 2 meets both statements. Either way, the school says late applications are still considered "as long as funds are available."

### Other out-of-date details on the aid section

- The FAQ still says Clarity "removes the need to upload your 2022 W2 and 1040 by transferring them directly from the IRS". The 2022 tax year is several years old.
- The guides the school links are labelled for 2025/2026. The Spanish Family Application Guide is the 2023–24 edition. None is the 2027–28 edition.

### How much aid, and how many families

**The school's own figure.** In its 2024–2025 Prep Fund results, Charlotte Prep says: "10% of Charlotte Prep families received tuition assistance."
- Sources: the "See The Impact of the 2024-2025 Prep Fund" section of https://charlotteprep.org/support/the-prep-fund, and the 2024–2025 Annual Report on Issuu (https://issuu.com/charlottepreparatoryschool/docs/2024-2025_annual_report).
- This counts families, not students. The number of families is not published.

**The IRS figure.** The school's federal tax returns report each year's aid as "Financial Aid", described as a "Reduction in tuition base" (Form 990, Schedule I). These are tax-return figures, not numbers the school publishes on its website.

| Fiscal year (July–June) | Total aid | Students aided |
|---|---|---|
| 2024–25 | $476,679 | 49 |
| 2023–24 | $457,393 | 50 |
| 2022–23 | $368,575 | 47 |
| 2021–22 | $363,160 | 48 |

The full eight-year series is in the Form 990 file. The return explains: "These funds are applied to the tuition balance and are not available for other uses."

The school does not publish an average award, the largest award, or a total aid budget.

### Merit scholarships

- **Charlotte Prep's current page:** aid is awarded partly on "academic merit", but no stand-alone merit scholarship is offered.
- **The Edward Ritter Scholarship, a past program.** The school's archived tuition pages from 2023 described it. Its guidelines document is still online at https://charlotteprep.org/uploads/files/Admissions/Ritter_Scholarship_Award_External_Guidelines.pdf.pdf, dated June 2022. It says: "Annually, one student new to Charlotte Preparatory School will be awarded free tuition and up to $1,000 toward school related expenses or fees (i.e., computer fees, books, class trips)." The award was renewable through 8th grade and required the family to qualify for aid.
- The scholarship is no longer mentioned on the tuition page; it was gone by November 2024. Its guidelines still refer to the school's previous aid system (SSS). Treat it as discontinued unless the school says otherwise.

### NC Opportunity Scholarship (state voucher)

Charlotte Prep's website does not mention the NC Opportunity Scholarship anywhere, and the school appears in none of the state's recent recipient lists.

The state publishes an annual list of every private school with Opportunity Scholarship recipients. Charlotte Preparatory School is not on any of the last four:

| School year | State report | Charlotte Prep listed? |
|---|---|---|
| 2024–25 | https://webservices.ncleg.gov/ViewDocSiteFile/102407 | No |
| 2023–24 | https://webservices.ncleg.gov/ViewDocSiteFile/91108 | No |
| 2022–23 | https://webservices.ncleg.gov/ViewDocSiteFile/81618 | No |
| 2021–22 | https://webservices.ncleg.gov/ViewDocSiteFile/72170 | No |

For comparison, the 2024–25 report lists Trinity Episcopal School (210 recipients) and Charlotte Christian School (608).

Being absent means no family used a voucher at Charlotte Prep in those years. It does not prove the school would refuse one. A family relying on the voucher should ask the school directly.

### Other ways families save

- **Sibling discount:** "We offer a 3% discount for younger siblings of current students."
- **Free sibling care:** "We provide complimentary care for younger students who have siblings with a later dismissal time."
- **Staff families:** "All full-time employees are eligible for a 50% tuition remission for their children (up to two)." (https://charlotteprep.org/about/employment)
- **Tuition Refund Plan:** required unless tuition is paid in full by May 1. See the Tuition and Fees file.

# Charlotte Preparatory School — Financial Aid and Tuition — Form 990

As a nonprofit, Charlotte Prep files an annual federal tax return (IRS Form 990) under the name "Charlotte Preparatory School Inc", EIN 45-2588411, 212 Boyce Rd, Charlotte. The returns show how much tuition the school collects, how much aid it gives, and what it pays its leaders. **Every figure on this page comes from those tax returns, not from the school's website.** The school's fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30. The most recent return covers the year ending June 30, 2025, and the IRS released it in 2026.

### Financial aid, year by year

Schedule I of the 990 reports aid to students as "Financial Aid". The value is described as a "Reduction in tuition base", and the return adds: "These funds are applied to the tuition balance and are not available for other uses."

| Fiscal year ending June | Aid total | Students aided | Average per student (our calculation) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | $476,679 | 49 | $9,728 |
| 2024 | $457,393 | 50 | $9,148 |
| 2023 | $368,575 | 47 | $7,842 |
| 2022 | $363,160 | 48 | $7,566 |
| 2021 | $516,135 | 58 | $8,899 |
| 2020 | $502,105 | 68 | $7,384 |
| 2019 | $448,646 | 61 | $7,355 |
| 2018 | $374,330 | 51 | $7,340 |

The average is the aid total divided by the number of students. The school does not publish it.

The number of students aided peaked at 68 in the year ending June 2020 and has held at 47–50 since 2022. Meanwhile the average award has grown, to $9,728 in the latest year. That is about a third of the 2026–27 Grades 1–4 tuition of $28,800.

Measured against tuition revenue, aid has run between 4% and 7% over these years (our calculation). The school's own statistic is that 10% of families received tuition assistance in 2024–25; see the Financial Support file.

### The school's finances, year by year

| Fiscal year ending June | Total revenue | Tuition and fees | Total expenses | Net assets at year end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | $15,824,777 | $11,048,536 | $11,260,242 | $20,051,494 |
| 2024 | $16,780,164 | $10,400,476 | $11,739,897 | $15,486,959 |
| 2023 | $9,564,533 | $9,210,336 | $8,710,752 | $10,446,692 |
| 2022 | $9,084,492 | $8,742,300 | $8,054,210 | $9,592,911 |
| 2021 | $8,078,522 | $6,920,082 | $6,947,278 | $8,562,629 |
| 2020 | $7,148,634 | $6,934,083 | $6,903,392 | $7,431,385 |
| 2019 | $7,401,105 | $7,113,057 | $7,125,217 | $7,186,143 |
| 2018 | $7,316,807 | $6,968,947 | $6,763,654 | $6,910,255 |

"Tuition and fees" is the return's only program-service revenue line. It is labelled "Tuition and Fees" and carries the IRS business code 611600.

Revenue jumped in the two most recent years for reasons beyond tuition. The 2024 return reports $4,961,877 of "Other" revenue that it does not explain further. The 2025 return reports $1,894,014 of "Insurance Proceeds" and $979,886 of "Other". Contributions were $1,187,398 in 2024 and $1,669,188 in 2025. For context, the school's 2024–2025 annual report says that "In the summer of 2023, … the lower school building was destroyed by a fire". It also says the lower school classrooms "will begin the 2025 school year in a beautiful new building". The tax returns do not connect the insurance proceeds or the "Other" revenue to the fire. The returns also show the school financed construction with tax-exempt bonds through the North Carolina Capital Facilities Finance Agency. This was the period when the new Lower School building went up. Year-end liabilities were $6,157,451 in 2024 and $14,344,547 in 2025.

### Older years (summary figures only)

| Fiscal year ending June | Total revenue | Total expenses | Total assets | Total liabilities |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | $7,080,338 | $6,424,602 | $18,596,755 | $12,239,653 |
| 2016 | $7,382,467 | $6,419,382 | $18,626,337 | $12,924,971 |
| 2015 | $7,694,728 | $6,573,686 | $18,341,034 | $13,449,725 |
| 2014 | $7,154,028 | $5,860,855 | $18,450,853 | $14,655,962 |
| 2013 | $6,368,180 | $5,498,663 | $17,934,296 | $15,393,547 |

### Head of school pay

| Fiscal year ending June | Name | Title on the return | Pay from the school | Other pay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | Chris Marblo | Ex-Officio | $346,133 | $15,431 |
| 2024 | Chris Marblo | Ex-Officio | $257,451 | $0 |
| 2023 | Chris Marblo | Ex-Officio | $212,172 | $0 |
| 2022 | Chris Marblo | Ex-Officio | $182,336 | $0 |
| 2021 | Eddie Mensah | Head of School | $81,078 | $0 |
| 2021 | Chris Marblo | Ex-Officio | $88,689 | $0 |
| 2020 | Eddie Mensah | Head of School | $157,500 | $3,150 |
| 2019 | Eddie Mensah | Head of School | $169,500 | $3,390 |
| 2018 | N Blair Fisher | Head of School | $95,718 | $1,950 |

How to read this:
- The returns title Chris Marblo "Ex-Officio", meaning his board seat. The school's own 2023–2024 annual report signs him as "Head of School".
- In the year ending June 2021, Eddie Mensah and Chris Marblo each received partial-year pay, consistent with a mid-year change of head. The two figures are not a pay cut.
- The year ending June 2018 also shows a change. N Blair Fisher is listed as Head of School, and Eddie Mensah is listed as Head of Middle at $120,000.
- The school's current head is **Todd Ballaban**, per the staff directory, the 2024–2025 annual report and his September 2025 letters to families. No return filed so far covers a year in which he was head.
- The school's 2024–2025 annual report says Chris Marblo "has served as Head of School at Charlotte Prep for the past five years" and "arrived in 2020". It wishes him "endless joy and adventure in retirement".
- The 2025 figure ($346,133 plus $15,431) covers his final year and is much higher than the year before. The return does not explain the increase, and this page does not guess at it.

The returns say head-of-school pay is set using "Data from comparable sized and types of schools (NAIS Benchmarks)".

### Staff size, as reported

The returns report total employees of 159 (2025), 146 (2024), 146 (2023), 137 (2022), 126 (2021), 128 (2020), 134 (2019) and 134 (2018). This counts everyone paid during the year, including part-time after-school and summer staff. It is not a teacher count.

# Charlotte Preparatory School — Financial Aid and Tuition — Tuition History

### Tuition by year

| School year | Kindergarten | Grades 1–4 | Grades 5–8 | After School Program (annual) | Drop-in after school |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2015–16 (page undated) | $16,860 | $17,800 | $18,350 | $3,400 K · $2,975 Gr 1–4 · $2,750 Gr 5–8 | $17.00/hour |
| 2016–17 (page undated) | $16,860 | $18,300 | $19,100 | $3,430 K · $3,025 Gr 1–4 · $2,800 Gr 5–8 | $17.70/hour |
| 2017–18 | $16,860 | $18,750 | $19,600 | $3,200 | $18.00/hour |
| 2018–19 | $17,350 | $19,300 | $20,200 | $3,300 | $18.00/hour |
| 2021–22 | $19,100 | $21,300 | $22,300 | $3,500 (also printed as $3,600) | $18.00/hour |
| 2023–24 | $21,300 | $23,800 | $25,000 | $4,000 | $20/hour |
| 2024–25 | $22,400 | $25,000 | $26,250 | $4,200 | $20/hour |
| 2026–27 | $25,800 | $28,800 | $30,200 | $4,500 | $20/hour |

Years 2019–20, 2020–21, 2022–23 and 2025–26 are missing because no archived copy of the school's tuition page survives for them.

### How fast tuition has risen (our calculation)

| Change | Kindergarten | Grades 1–4 | Grades 5–8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2015–16 → 2016–17 | 0% | +3% | +4% |
| 2016–17 → 2017–18 | 0% | +2% | +3% |
| 2017–18 → 2018–19 | +3% | +3% | +3% |
| 2018–19 → 2021–22 (three years) | +10% | +10% | +10% |
| 2021–22 → 2023–24 (two years) | +12% | +12% | +12% |
| 2023–24 → 2024–25 | +5% | +5% | +5% |
| 2024–25 → 2026–27 (two years) | +15% | +15% | +15% |
| 2015–16 → 2026–27 (eleven years) | +53% | +62% | +65% |

These percentages are our own arithmetic on the school's published prices, not figures the school publishes.

Before 2019, Charlotte Prep raised tuition about 2–4% a year. From 2021–22 on the pace picked up to roughly 5–7% a year. The two years from 2024–25 to 2026–27 added 15%, about 7% a year.

Two things changed alongside the prices. From 2024–25 the school folded its athletics, fine arts and technology fees into tuition, so part of that year's rise replaced fees families used to pay separately. Before-school care from 7:30 a.m. was free through 2021–22; by 2023–24 the page said "No additional before school care is available at this time."

### Montessori Early School, morning and school-day programs

| School year | Pre-Primary, to noon | Primary, to noon | Transitional K, to 2:30 | Montessori K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2015–16 (page undated) | $10,950 (Pre-Primary and Primary) | $10,950 | $14,900 | not offered on page |
| 2016–17 (page undated) | $11,250 (Pre-Primary and Primary) | $11,250 | $14,900 | not offered on page |
| 2017–18 | $11,500 | $12,000 | $15,500 | $16,860 |
| 2018–19 | $11,850 | $12,400 | $16,000 | $17,350 |
| 2021–22 | $13,100 | $13,700 | $17,700 | $19,100 |
| 2023–24 | $14,650 | $15,300 | $19,750 | $21,300 |
| 2024–25 | $15,400 | $16,100 | $20,750 | $22,400 |
| 2026–27 | $17,700 | $18,500 | $23,900 | $25,800 |

Until 2024–25 the Early School also sold year-round and school-year extended-day versions at a single all-in price. For 2026–27 the school instead sells the school-year program plus a separate Extended Day add-on, and no year-round option is listed.

# Charlotte Preparatory School — Financial Aid and Tuition — Tuition and Fees

Everything below is the school's "Tuition and fees for 2026-2027" page (https://charlotteprep.org/admissions/tuition-fees), copied line for line on October 19, 2026. Prices are for the 2026–27 school year.

### Tuition by program, 2026–27

**Montessori Early School.** The school notes: "Tuition below covers the school year only."

| Program | Hours | Tuition |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-Primary | 8:30 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. | $17,700 |
| Primary | 8:30 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. | $18,500 |
| Transitional Kindergarten | 8:30 a.m. - 2:30 p.m. | $23,900 |
| Montessori Kindergarten | 8:30 a.m. - 3:00 p.m. | $25,800 |

**Lower School (Kindergarten–4th Grade)**

| Grade | Tuition |
|---|---|
| Kindergarten | $25,800 |
| 1st - 4th Grades | $28,800 |

**Middle School**

| Grade | Tuition |
|---|---|
| 5th - 8th Grades | $30,200 |

Charlotte Prep prices by band, not by grade. One price covers Grades 1–4 and one covers Grades 5–8. Montessori Kindergarten and traditional Kindergarten cost the same, $25,800.

### Longer days for the Early School (add-ons)

| Add-on | Hours | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-Primary/Primary School Day* | 12:00 p.m. - 2:30/3:00 p.m. | $3,400 |
| Pre-Primary/Primary Extended Day | 12:00 p.m. - 5:30 p.m. | $5,900 |
| Transitional Kindergarten Extended Day | 2:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m. | $2,700 |

*The school's footnote: "Pre-Primary/Primary School Day option is only available for students with siblings enrolled at Prep in TK-8th grade."

So a 2- or 3-year-old with no older sibling at Prep can attend either half days or the full Extended Day, which runs to 5:30. There is no middle option.

### After School (Kindergarten–8th Grade)

| Option | Price |
|---|---|
| After School Program, Kindergarten - 8th Grade (3:00 p.m.- 5:30 p.m.) | $4,500 |
| Drop-in After School | $20/hour |

The school says drop-in "is available for $20/hour for Montessori Kindergarten through 8th Grade students." The Lower and Middle School sections of the page also list the program as "After School Program (Pickup by 5:30 p.m.) - $4,500".

### Fees and other costs, word for word

| Item | Amount | School's wording |
|---|---|---|
| Annual Down Payment | $2,000 | "Upon acceptance to Charlotte Preparatory School, a non-refundable down payment of $2,000, accompanied by a signed contract, secures an academic placement for an eligible student. This deposit is then credited to the overall tuition." |
| Parents' Association Fund | $150 per student, every year | "A fee of $150 per student is charged annually to fund the activities of our Parents' Association" |
| One-time New Family Commitment Fee | $1,000, once | "We require new families to submit this one-time payment of $1,000 upon signing their first tuition contract with Charlotte Preparatory School." |
| Tuition Refund Plan (TRP) | "approximately 1.45% of tuition cost" | "required unless the full annual fees are paid by May 1, in which case the plan is elective." |
| Hot lunch | Not published | Ordered and paid directly through FLIK Independent School Dining |
| Field trips | Not published | "Field trip fees may be assessed if needed." |

The school gives the TRP only as "approximately 1.45%" of tuition, with no dollar amount. At that rate, the TRP on $28,800 tuition would be about $418. That is our own estimate, not a school figure.

### Discounts and free care

- "We offer a 3% discount for younger siblings of current students."
- "We provide complimentary care for younger students who have siblings with a later dismissal time."
- Early drop-off: "You may drop off Early School students as early as 8:00 a.m., and lower and middle school students as early as 7:45 a.m. No additional before-school care is available at this time."

### What a first year costs (our calculation)

These add up only the figures the school publishes for 2026–27. They leave out lunch, field trips, the TRP and anything else the school does not price.

| Child entering | Tuition | Parents' Association | New Family Commitment Fee | First-year total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kindergarten | $25,800 | $150 | $1,000 | $26,950 |
| Grades 1–4 | $28,800 | $150 | $1,000 | $29,950 |
| Grades 5–8 | $30,200 | $150 | $1,000 | $31,350 |
| Add the After School Program | +$4,500 | | | |

The $2,000 down payment is not extra. It counts toward tuition.

### What tuition now includes

The school's strategic plan says three former add-on fees are now part of tuition: "We have included the fees for athletics, fine arts, and technology in tuition for the 2024-25 school year and will continue to do so moving forward. Other fees, which are mainly for optional activities, will still be billed separately." (https://charlotteprep.org/about/strategic-plan-2022-2027)

The same plan says the board compares tuition with nearby peer schools every year "to keep tuition at or below the median of peer schools while still investing in impactful programs and school needs."

### How to pay

The 2026–27 page does not say how payments are processed. Pages archived through 2021–22 named FACTS Management as the processor for full or monthly payment. The 2021–22 page added: "FACTS account fee is $20 for full payment and incidentals processing, or $50 for monthly payment and incidentals processing." The current page carries neither line.
